extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys and USPTO disciplinary staff (practitioners subject to USPTO professional responsibility rules)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, standards, and procedural criteria governing disciplinary actions against patent practitioners before the USPTO, including grounds for discipline, reporting duties, sanction structure (stay/suspension/probation), and procedures for enforcing probation. Focused on how the OED and USPTO Director handle and publish practitioner discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. § 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order is issued under statutory and regulatory authority specified above; disciplinary actions are resolved by agreement and approved by the Under Secretary/Director under those authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Disciplinary Rules to registered practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered patent attorneys are subject to the USPTO Disciplinary Rules set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At all times relevant, Respondent, as a registered practitioner, is bound by the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility and its provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for discipline: suspension by a State on ethical grounds (37 C.F.R. §10.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and (b), via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5), occurs when a practitioner is suspended from practice as an attorney on ethical grounds by any duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A State suspension for ethical reasons is itself actionable under the USPTO rules and can form the legal basis for USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner reporting duty for state discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must report discipline imposed by state bars to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED); Respondent timely reported the Texas discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related citation: practitioners remain subject to duties such as those in 37 C.F.R. § 11.14(a). The Final Order also requires Respondent to report any revocation of his probation in Texas to the OED Director within thirty days of revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of misconduct warranting discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Misconduct cited includes: failing to keep a client reasonably informed about the status of her legal matter; failing to explain matters sufficiently to permit informed client decisions; neglecting matters entrusted to the attorney; knowingly offering or using evidence the attorney knew to be false; engaging in dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific factual failures were the basis for state discipline and are identified as types of conduct that violate professional responsibility standards enforceable by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction components: suspension, stayed suspension, and probation
rubrics_metrics.description: The imposed sanction: suspension for thirty-six (36) months from practice before the USPTO, with the entirety of the suspension stayed, and a probationary period of thirty-six (36) months beginning on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The stay allows the practitioner to continue practicing before the Office during probation unless later suspended; the Final Order sets these temporal sanction parameters explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition permitting continued practice during probation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is permitted to practice patent, trademark, and non-patent law before the USPTO during his probationary period unless he is subsequently suspended or excluded by order of the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization to practice is contingent on complying with the Final Order and disciplinary rules; subsequent disciplinary action can revoke that permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirement for revocation of state probation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall report any revocation of his probation in Texas to the OED Director within thirty days of the revocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely notice of changed status in state discipline is required to the OED to enable USPTO action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause procedure for alleged probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes the practitioner failed to comply with the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule during probation, the OED Director shall: (A) issue an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not lift the stay and immediately suspend the practitioner for up to thirty-six months; (B) send the Order to the practitioner's last address of record per 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a); and (C) grant the practitioner fifteen (15) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the 15-day response period and consideration of any response, if the OED Director remains of that opinion, the OED Director forwards the Order to Show Cause, any response, and supporting argument/evidence to the USPTO Director requesting lifting of the stay and immediate suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if stay is lifted and suspension imposed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director lifts the stay and immediately suspends the practitioner: (1) the USPTO shall promptly dissociate the practitioner's name from all USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates; (2) the practitioner shall not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until reinstated; and (3) the practitioner may not obtain a USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissociation of electronic credentials and customer numbers is a direct operational consequence of suspension to prevent further practice before reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room on the USPTO web page and shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette containing specified information about the suspension, probation, underlying facts, and legal bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice template in the Final Order shows content to be published (practitioner name, registration number, nature and length of sanction, summary of underlying misconduct and state discipline, statutory/regulatory authorities). Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted at the OED Reading Room URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office's reserved rights to seek further discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from seeking discipline against the practitioner under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34 through 11.57 for the misconduct that caused the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement does not waive the Office's ability to pursue additional enforcement actions under the specified procedures and rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, when addressing further complaints or evidence of the same/similar misconduct or in any future disciplinary proceeding concerning the practitioner as an aggravating factor and/or to rebut any statement by or on the practitioner's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior discipline can be used substantively in later proceedings affecting sanctions or credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs between parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement specifies that each side bears its own costs rather than awarding costs against the practitioner or the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: State bar probation conditions that supported probated state suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: The Texas State Bar, District No.4 Grievance Committee ordered a three-year fully probated suspension subject to multiple conditions: (i) Respondent not violate any term of the judgment; (ii) Respondent not engage in professional misconduct; (iii) Respondent not violate any state or federal criminal statutes; (iv) Respondent keep the State Bar of Texas informed of his current address; (v) Respondent comply with Minimum Continuing Legal Education requirements for Texas; (vi) Respondent comply with Texas State IOLTA requirements; (vii) Respondent promptly respond to any request for information from the Texas State Bar; (viii) Respondent pay attorney's fees to the Texas State Bar; and (ix) Respondent complete three additional hours of Ethics CLE in addition to the minimum CLE requirements, within a time set by the Grievance Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the explicit conditions the State Bar attached to its probation; failure to comply with such conditions could lead to revocation of the probated suspension and are relevant to USPTO consideration where state discipline is the basis for USPTO action.
